# Lungs: mechanics, ventilation–perfusion, pathology

[All modules](README.md) · [Known misses](../validation/known-misses.md#lungs) · 19 source files, 2779 lines · 39 test files

## Purpose

<!-- hand:purpose -->
The lungs model the respiratory system's mechanics and gas mixing: four alveolar units (left and right, fast and slow)
behind one airway and one chest wall, per-lung perfusion with hypoxic pulmonary vasoconstriction, atelectasis and
recruitment, and the mixing point that turns each unit's ventilation–perfusion balance into arterial and end-tidal
gases. Lung diseases are a data catalogue of graded effects on these parameters. A clinician-educator reads it to see
why plateau pressure, compliance, shunt or EtCO2 change with a condition; an embedding developer reads it for the
per-breath mechanics and the per-lung PVR it hands to the circulation.
<!-- /hand:purpose -->

## Equations in words

<!-- hand:equations -->
- Each of the four alveolar units has a Venegas sigmoid pressure–volume curve in transpulmonary pressure,
  V(P) = a + b/(1 + e^(−(P − c)/d)), with d chosen so its slope at c equals the unit's compliance (Venegas, Harris &
  Simon 1998; `l2/lung/params.ts`, `l2/lung/venegas.ts`), and its own inspiratory and expiratory airway resistance;
  the units share one linear chest wall and are driven by a flow source, a pressure source or a closed airway
  (tables §4.3; `l2/lung/mechanics.ts`).
- Per-breath mechanics are measured as a clinician measures them, on a copy of the unit state: PEEPi = PEEPtot − set
  PEEP, driving pressure = Pplat − PEEPtot, Cstat = VT/(Pplat − PEEPtot), Cdyn = VT/(Ppeak − PEEPtot) and
  Rinsp = (Ppeak − Pplat)/inspiratory flow (Hess & Kacmarek ch. 3; `l2/lung/breath.ts`, `l2/lung/measure.ts`).
- Oesophageal pressure is an estimate: the model's pleural pressure when awake and spontaneous, and a supine baseline
  that rises with BMI plus the chest-wall recoil when ventilated or anaesthetised (West ch. 7; Owens et al. 2012;
  `l2/lung/breath.ts`).
- Each lung's blood flow divides into a collapsed part (true shunt), an aerated-but-hypoxic part and a normal part;
  hypoxic pulmonary vasoconstriction scales the first two, and the same factor is that side's PVR multiplier for the
  circulation (tables §4.2, catalogue §22; `l2/lung/perfusion.ts`, `l2/lung/circ-link.ts`).
- Atelectasis has three pools per lung: induction and absorption collapse with the Rothen time constant (faster at
  high FiO2, slower with PEEP), collapse behind a blocked bronchus with τ = 5 + 40·(inert fraction/0.79) min, and a
  condition's recruitable collapse that opens with inspiratory pressure and closes towards what PEEP keeps open
  (tables §4.1, catalogue §6, §22–§23; `l2/lung/recruit.ts`).
- On the O2 side, arterial content is the flow-weighted end-capillary contents plus shunt at mixed-venous content,
  with one alveolar O2 store per lung so each side desaturates at its own rate (tables §4.1, §4.5;
  `l2/lung/mix-o2.ts`).
- On the CO2 side, each ventilated unit's alveolar PCO2 follows its own V/Q, the arterial PCO2 is the
  perfusion-weighted mix, and end-tidal PCO2 is the expiratory-flow-weighted mix at end-expiration, diluted by
  unperfused alveolar ventilation (tables §4.4; `l2/lung/mix-co2.ts`); the end-tidal ratio relaxes with the alveolar
  CO2 time constant, about 6 s ventilated in a healthy adult (`l2/lung/lung.ts`).
- Spontaneous minute ventilation is a CO2 response above an apnoeic threshold, multiplied by a Weil-form hypoxic
  factor, reduced by opioid and hypnotic depression and by fatigue, plus pain and J-receptor terms (Weil 1970,
  tables §4.6; `l2/lung/drive.ts`).
- Spirometry is computed from the units' emptying: FEV1 and FVC sum each unit's vital capacity times its exponential
  emptying at 1 s and at the end of the test (ATS/ERS 2019; `l2/lung/volumes.ts`).
- A lung condition's effect at severity s is 1 + (v − 1)·s for a multiplier, v·s for an additive effect, or a move
  from the healthy default towards v, or piecewise-linear severity knots; stacked conditions multiply, add (shunt
  capped at 0.6, atelectasis at 0.7) or take the largest departure (catalogue §33, after Pulse's severity tables;
  `data/lung-pathology.ts`, `l2/lung/conditions.ts`).

In the near-fatal range (severity 1.0 → 1.25, reached through the airway `bronchospasm` alias) the lumen fills with mucosal oedema and mucus plugs rather than tone (extensive luminal plugging in fatal asthma: Kuyper et al. 2003 Am J Med 115:6), so the reversible share falls to (1 − REFRACT_SEV) of itself at 1.25 [ENG 0.6]. DURATION. A slow-onset attack — hours of inflammation, oedema and plugging — responds less and more slowly to a β2 agonist than a sudden-onset, mostly bronchospastic one (McFadden 2003 AJRCCM 168:740; Rodrigo & Rodrigo 2000 Chest 118:1547; Rodrigo, Rodrigo & Hall 2004 Chest 125:1081), so the share decays toward (1 − REFRACT_DUR_MAX) of itself with τ REFRACT_TAU_MIN [ENG 0.9 and 360 min (the 6 h slow-onset boundary); fit target: a non-responder — a 12 h severe asthma improves < 15 % with a saturating β2 dose (measured −14 %) — and every fresh arm keeping ≥ 95 % of `frac` (0.963 at 15 min)]. The age is sim time since the condition appeared plus the spec's `ageMin` (the attack's age when it was sent), so status asthmaticus is one command: `lungCondition asthma 1, ageMin 720` keeps ≈ 0.7 · 0.22 ≈ 0.16 of its airway obstruction reversible. This adds NO dose-response of its own — B is the drug model's; this function is the MAXIMUM reversal. A drug-driven bronchospasm severity — histamine release (morphine, atracurium, mivacurium) and anaphylactic mediators act on the SAME smooth muscle `relaxed()` relieves, so the drug's contribution is an added SEVERITY on the `bronchospasm` spec, not a second state. 0.35 at full histamine [ENG; direction: M10 ch. 22 / ch. 24 (wheeze and bronchospasm after a fast benzylisoquinolinium or morphine bolus), size has no source]. A plain scalable input: a future per-profile airway-reactivity gain (research/19) multiplies it in one place. |

The carotid body's drive is not only a gain on the CO2 error: at a PCO2 under the apnoeic threshold a hypoxic subject's CO2 response does not fall to zero but flattens onto a PO2-dependent PLATEAU (the "dog-leg" of Nielsen & Smith 1952 Acta Physiol Scand 24:293; Lumb, Nunn's Applied Respiratory Physiology 8e ch. 5), so a hypoxaemic patient whose PaCO2 sits under the (post-induction, raised) threshold still breathes. The plateau is HVR_INDEP_VE × resting VE × (H(PaO2) − 1), depressed by hvrDep exactly like the multiplicative arm, and the chemical drive is max(fan, plateau): above the threshold the fan is larger, so every existing hypoxic-response band is unchanged; at normoxia the plateau is < 0.02 × resting VE (below the apnoea threshold). | CVP ≥ 15 mmHg | 11.5 | — | TOO NARROW ([audit row 51](../../docs/validation/target-audit/30-target-audit.md#row-51)) | CVP >= 10 mmHg (or >= baseline + 5) | [`obstructive-aliases.test.ts`](../../packages/engine-core/test/engine/obstructive-aliases.test.ts) |
